title: Chat Client with the Foundry SDK
group: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55-60%)

header.html: Implement AI solutions by using Microsoft Foundry (55–60%)
Create a lightweight chat client application by using the Foundry SDK
the official AI-901 study guide, skills measured as of April 15, 2026

html:
1The idea

A chat client application is a small program that sends a prompt to a deployed model and prints the reply. The Foundry SDK gives you the Python (and C#, JavaScript, Java) building blocks. The exam wants you to read a short program and say what each part does.

Step What the code does
1. Sign in Uses your Microsoft Entra ID identity through DefaultAzureCredential
2. Connect Creates a project client with the project endpoint
3. Get a model client Asks the project client for an OpenAI-compatible client
4. Send the prompt Calls the model by its deployment name with your input
5. Read the reply Prints the output text

2Install and sign in

  • Install the SDK with pip install "azure-ai-projects>=2.3.0". The sample uses DefaultAzureCredential, which comes from the azure-identity package.
  • Azure AI Projects 2.x is not compatible with 1.x: sample code for the older version looks different. [Verify live]
  • Sign in first with the Azure CLI command az login; DefaultAzureCredential then picks up your sign-in. No key is written into the code.
Exam tip

. "No secret in the source code" → DefaultAzureCredential with Microsoft Entra ID. The identity needs permission on the project.

Exam tip

. No secret in the source code: DefaultAzureCredential uses your Microsoft Entra ID sign-in (after az login).

3The program

This is the short program from the Microsoft quickstart. Read it line by line.

from azure.identity import DefaultAzureCredential
from azure.ai.projects import AIProjectClient

FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT = "your_project_endpoint"

project = AIProjectClient(
    endpoint=FOUNDRY_PROJECT_ENDPOINT,
    credential=DefaultAzureCredential(),
)
openai = project.get_openai_client()

response = openai.responses.create(
    model="gpt-5-mini",
    input="What is the size of France in square miles?",
)
print(f"Response output: {response.output_text}")
Line Meaning
AIProjectClient(endpoint=..., credential=...) Connects to the Foundry project with your identity
project.get_openai_client() Returns an OpenAI-compatible client for models in the project
openai.responses.create(...) Sends the request using the Responses API
model="gpt-5-mini" The deployment name of the model you deployed
input="..." The user prompt
response.output_text The text of the reply
  • The endpoint looks like https://resource_name.services.ai.azure.com/api/projects/project_name.
  • The model value must match a deployment in the project. A wrong name gives an error that the deployment was not found.
  • To set the assistant's behavior you add instructions (a system prompt). Beyond the study guide for the exact parameter.
  • For a multi-turn chat, the app keeps the earlier messages and sends them again (Module 2). Check the sample code for the exact input format. [Verify live]
Exam tip

. Identify the parts: client creation (endpoint plus credential), model call (deployment name plus input), output (output_text). A question may ask what to change to use another model (change the deployment name) or another project (change the endpoint).

4Common mistakes

Symptom Likely cause
Authentication error Not signed in (az login) or no permission on the project
"Deployment not found" The model value does not match a deployment name
Reply cut off Max output tokens too low
Works in the playground, fails in code Wrong endpoint or a different project
Sample code from an old tutorial fails SDK version 1.x code with a 2.x package

5Exam Q&A

5.1 Practice questions (choose the best answer)

S1A Fabrikam Outdoors developer wants Python code to authenticate without storing a key in the source file. What should the code use?

  • AA password stored in a text file next to the code
  • BDefaultAzureCredential with the signed-in identity
  • CThe deployment name used as a password
  • DThe playground URL pasted into the code
Show the answer

Answer: B. DefaultAzureCredential uses Microsoft Entra ID sign-in, so no secret is stored in the code.

S2In the sample program, what does AIProjectClient(endpoint=..., credential=...) do?

  • ADeploys a new model to the project
  • BPrints the reply to the screen
  • CConnects the program to the Foundry project
  • DDeletes the project and its models
Show the answer

Answer: C. It creates the client that connects to the project through its endpoint.

S3A call fails because the deployment cannot be found. What should the developer check?

  • AThat the model value matches the deployment name in the project
  • BThe color theme of the Foundry portal
  • CThe number of subscriptions in the tenant
  • DThe temperature of the model
Show the answer

Answer: A. The model parameter must be the name of a deployment in the project.

S4Which property of the response object holds the text answer in the sample?

  • Aresponse.endpoint_url
  • Bresponse.credential_name
  • Cresponse.project_name
  • Dresponse.output_text
Show the answer

Answer: D. The sample prints response.output_text.

S5The team deploys a second model named chat-small and wants the program to use it. What is the smallest change?

  • AChange the endpoint to another country
  • BRewrite the program in another language
  • CRemove DefaultAzureCredential
  • DChange the model value to chat-small
Show the answer

Answer: D. The model value is the deployment name, so changing it selects another deployment.

S6Which command signs in so that DefaultAzureCredential can find your identity during development?

  • Apip uninstall
  • Baz login
  • Caz group delete
  • Dgit push
Show the answer

Answer: B. The quickstart says to sign in with the Azure CLI az login command first.

5.2 Recall questions

R1Which Python package provides the Foundry project client?

Show the answer

azure-ai-projects.

R2Which class connects to a project?

Show the answer

AIProjectClient.

R3Which method returns an OpenAI-compatible client?

Show the answer

get_openai_client.

R4Which value in the call is the deployment name?

Show the answer

The model argument.

R5Where is the answer text in the response?

Show the answer

output_text.

R6Which authentication class avoids storing a key in code?

Show the answer

DefaultAzureCredential.

6Quick Reference Card

Topic Key fact
Steps sign in, connect, get client, send the prompt, read the reply
Packages azure-ai-projects (2.x) and azure-identity
Connect AIProjectClient(endpoint, credential=DefaultAzureCredential())
Call project.get_openai_client(); openai.responses.create(model=deployment, input=prompt)
Read response.output_text
Troubleshoot az login, permission, deployment name, endpoint, token limit
